name: Rice-paper & cheese bake — all-yellow variant (cottage + 130 g 9%)

source.author: Calculated variant of the logged batch
source.notes: Leaner variant of rice_paper_cheese_bake_logged: the cheddar is dropped and the whole 130 g of hard cheese is 9% light yellow. CALCULATED, not yet cooked. TOTAL batch = 3 rice-paper sheets (~33 g) + 250 g cottage cheese + 130 g of 9% light yellow cheese. Makes 2 units; macros below are PER UNIT (batch ÷ 2). ASSUMPTIONS: ~½ of one beaten egg sticking as the wash + ~3 g sesame, no added salt. Estimate.

serving_desc: 1 unit (~200 g cooked) — the batch makes 2

ingredients.note: replaces the 75 g yellow + 55 g cheddar of the logged batch

steps: Mix the cottage and 9% yellow cheese; season with pepper.
On parchment layer: rice paper → half the cheese → rice paper → rest of cheese → rice paper on top.
Brush both sides with beaten egg, sprinkle sesame.
Bake at 200 °C for 25–30 min until golden and crispy; cut into 2 units.

batch_totals.note: Whole batch (2 units), incl. assumed ~½ egg wash + ~3 g sesame. Vs the cheddar batch: same protein, ~37 fewer kcal and ~5 g less fat PER UNIT, because 9% cheese carries far less fat than 28% cheddar.

him.verdict: The leanest, highest-density version of this bake and a top-tier cut snack — ~33 g protein per unit for only 350 kcal is ~9.4 g protein per 100 kcal, right up with the best in your library. Swapping the 28%-fat cheddar for 9% cheese keeps the protein identical while cutting ~5 g fat and ~3 g saturated fat per unit vs the batch you actually made. Only reasons it's not a 10: still near-zero fiber and high sodium (~800 mg/unit), both inherent to the dish. The one thing you lose vs the cheddar version is flavor depth — worth a pinch of za'atar/paprika.
flags: ~33 g protein / unit at 350 kcal — ~9.4 g protein per 100 kcal (excellent)
leaner than the cheddar batch: ~5 g less fat, ~3 g less saturated fat per unit
high sodium (~800 mg/unit) from the cheeses
suggested_mods: Best cut version of this bake — make this over the cheddar one on deficit days
Add za'atar / oregano / smoked paprika to the cheese to replace the cheddar's punch
Serve with tomato/salad for the fiber + vitamin C it lacks

her_preconception.verdict: Same clean preconception profile as the cheddar batch — fully baked, all pasteurized cheeses (cottage + 9% yellow), no soft/brined cheese, no safety flags. Strong protein and calcium; leaning out the fat doesn't change her lens either way. Still not a folate/iron/DHA source, so it's a good snack rather than a prenatal main.
prenatal_highlights: some choline from the egg wash
fully baked, all pasteurized cheeses — no safety flags
suggested_mods: Pair with salad/tomato for folate + vitamin C
Fine as-is; no swaps needed for safety

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-09-25 as a reference variant (may use in future). Leanest version of the rice-paper cheese bake: per unit ~350 kcal, 33 g protein, 14 g fat (~9.4 g protein/100 kcal). Batch = 3 rice papers + 250 g cottage + 130 g of 9% yellow, makes 2 units. Prefer this over the cheddar batch on cutting days; pair with tomato/salad for fiber.
cooking_guide: Mix the cottage and grated 9% yellow cheese with pepper until fairly even; it's a wet, cottage-forward mix, which helps the rice paper soften and seal.
Keep the rice papers DRY (don't soak). Line a tray with parchment.
Layer: rice paper → half the cheese (leave a ~1 cm border) → rice paper → rest of the cheese → rice paper on top. Press gently all over to seal.
Brush the top with beaten egg (gives the deep-golden, shatter-crisp surface), scatter sesame, then carefully flip and brush + sesame the other side too.
Bake in a fully preheated oven at 200 °C (400 °F) for 25–30 min. With no cheddar it's a touch less greasy, so watch it crisps evenly — flip once around 15 min if browning unevenly.
Pull it deep golden and crackly; rice paper burns fast, so watch the last 5 min.
Rest 2–3 min on a rack, then cut into 2 units with a serrated knife.

Tip: since there's no cheddar and no salt, lean on seasoning — za'atar, oregano, smoked paprika or a grating of garlic in the cheese brings back the flavor; a spoon of cooked spinach folded in adds a little fiber.
